 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Brooks Koepka admits that watching international team golf from the sidelines makes him angry. The 36-year-old star wants to return to the Ryder Cup in 2027. He told reporters that missing these big moments "kind of infuriates me sitting on the sidelines." This feeling drives his push to get his game back on track.
 His return to the PGA Tour in 2026 has been rough so far. Koepka missed the FedEx Cup Playoffs and struggled with consistency. He even called his own season "pathetic" earlier this year. Yet he feels good about the welcome he got from other players. "I felt very at peace with coming back," Koepka said recently, according to ClutchPoints . "The reception was fantastic from all the players, caddies, just everybody on tour."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Adare Manor Is The Goal
 The 2027 Ryder Cup will be held at Adare Manor in Ireland. Koepka has made this event his main target for next season. He spoke ahead of the RSM Classic about his plans. He knows he needs better results to earn a spot on the team.
 Jim Furyk will captain the American side. Furyk is already talking about changes to how the team plays. Koepka has been a key player in past Ryder Cups, competing in 2016, 2018, 2021, and 2023. He was left off the 2025 team and missed the 2026 Presidents Cup too. The frustration of being on the bench is real for a man who loves to compete for his country.
 Why The Fight Matters
 Koepka believes the field would be tougher if LIV Golf stars were still on the PGA Tour. He thinks Scottie Scheffler's dominant 2024 run would have faced more resistance. He knows what it takes to win on the biggest stages.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He is working hard to fix his swing and change his coaching setup. The goal is to rediscover the form that made him a five-time major champion. Koepka is competing at the RSM Classic this week as the 2026 season wraps up.
